subject: FreshPeak commercial structure — dedicated/VPC pilot & pricing ask
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@freshpeak.health>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial structure question: dedicated + VPC pilot

Markus — thanks again for the demo this morning. FreshPeak is excited about Redwood's latency profile but we need a commercial structure that aligns with our procurement windows and compliance needs. Two asks on our side: 1) pilot pricing for 3 months on a small dedicated pool + VPC control plane, and 2) an onboarding credit to offset migration engineering.

High level numbers we discussed on the call: target list price ~$1.2M ARR equivalent for committed capacity, but procurement is pushing for a 30–40% discount in year one given the pilot risk and our multi-product roadmap. They're also requesting a 60-day payment term and an explicit SOC2 plus SOC2 audit evidence package timeline.

Can you share what kind of commercial exception you'd need to make this happen (discount ceiling, upfront credits, term structure)? We can loop in procurement if that helps.

— Alex
Senior Director, IT & Cloud
FreshPeak Health
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Commercial structure question: dedicated + VPC pilot

Kimberly / Karthik — forwarding FreshPeak's ask. TL;DR: strategic healthcare prospect, looking to commit to a dedicated pool (multi-year potential) but asking for an aggressive year-one concession: 30–40% off list plus onboarding credits and extended T&Cs (60-day pay). They explicitly want VPC control plane (private deployment) for the pilot.

Why this matters: fresh product reference in NE region, potential to scale across multiple lines of business. Deal team thinks anchored ARR around $1.2M list, with a realistic first-year commitment closer to $800–900k if we give the concession. We can propose a stepped discount (35% year 1, 20% year 2) with a minimum committed GPU-hours floor and a 2-year minimum to protect revenue.

Request: need VP/CFO signoff on a one-time price exception and onboarding credits. Attached is a draft term sheet (v3) with our recommended guardrails.

Attachments: FreshPeak_TermSheet_v3.pdf (commercial redline), FreshPeak_SOW_outline.docx (statement of work highlights)

Can you advise whether we can approve under delegated authority or if we should route to exec committee? If delegated, what's the cap we can sign for?

— Markus
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Commercial structure question: dedicated + VPC pilot

Markus — thanks for the quick summary. A few clarifying items before I can sign off: 1) please confirm the minimum committed spend floor (monthly GPU-hours or $) and the penalty/true-up mechanics if FreshPeak underuses capacity; 2) what guardrails are in the term sheet for early termination (refunds of credits, prorated charges); 3) why do we need to give 60-day payment terms rather than standard net30? Procurement's ask to stretch to net60 increases cash conversion risk — can Sales propose a mid-ground (e.g., net45 with ACH milestone)?

Also want to see model-level alternatives: can we offer a quantized variant (lower-cost model) for year 1 as an alternate to a straight steeper discount? That would preserve ASP while addressing their cost sensitivity.

If the ask is a 35% upfront concession plus $80k onboarding credit with a 2-year minimum and a $400k committed spend floor, that is material and needs VP + CFO delegation confirmed. If you think this is strategically necessary to land region reference, include the ARR expansion thesis and churn mitigations.

— Kim
VP Finance (Commercial)
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Commercial structure question: dedicated + VPC pilot

Kim / Karthik — answers inline and updated ask. I also attached a short customer-impact memo and the redlined term sheet (v3) with explicit guardrails.

1) Commit floor: propose $375k committed spend (annualized) with monthly true-up using a 30% overage credit to protect ramp variability. If FreshPeak under-uses by >40% for a rolling quarter, they pay a shortfall true-up equal to 50% of the missed commit for that quarter — this discourages under-provisioning while giving them room to ramp.

2) Early termination: onboarding credit of $80k is repayable on a straight-line basis over 12 months if they terminate early (prorated). Any unused prepaid capacity is refundable only to the extent we can re-deploy within 90 days.

3) Payment terms: propose net45 with a milestone-triggered 30% invoicing at kick-off to reduce cash risk. Procurement insisted on net60; net45 is a compromise.

4) Alternate to discount: we can offer a quantized model family for year 1 (approx ~18% unit cost reduction) combined with a 15% list discount — this is less dilutive to ASP but requires engineering validation for quality. I flagged this with product and they said a bench validation will take ~2 weeks.

Proposed commercial concession summary: 35% discount year1, 20% year2; $80k onboarding credit (repayable prorated 12 months); $375k commit floor (annualized) with true-up; net45 payment terms with 30% kick-off invoice.

Why approve: FreshPeak is an integrated procurement and provider partner in NE — landing them as a reference unlocks cross-sell into two partner hospitals plus potential marketplace listing. We forecast expansion to $2.5–3M ARR over 36 months with moderate churn risk if we secure the pilot.

Request: Kimberly, can you confirm whether this fits within your delegated approval threshold? If not, I recommend we route to the pricing committee (Karthik + Finance + Legal) for next-day review. I can pull together a short exec memo if needed.

— Markus
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Commercial structure question: dedicated + VPC pilot — approval

Markus / Karthik — I reviewed the proposed guardrails and the ARR expansion thesis. Given the strategic upside and the protections you've built in (repayable onboarding credit, commit floor, stronger true-up), I'm comfortable approving this as a one-time commercial exception under my delegation. Conditions: 1) Procurement gets net45 with 30% kick-off invoice (no net60), 2) the onboarding credit language is included in the MSA with the 12-month clawback, and 3) we use the quantized model as an explicit fallback in the contract to limit unit cost downside.

Please proceed to finalize the term sheet and coordinate signature with FreshPeak. Copy legal on the final MSA redline and include a short cover memo to execs summarizing commercial impact and 36-month revenue thesis.

Kimberly Park
VP Finance (Commercial) — signoff granted
Redwood Inference
